I give up. The theorem as stated is false, so it can't be proved.

`IsTree T1` and `IsTree T2` are statements about graphs on the whole vertex type `V`, so each of `T1` and `T2` must be connected on all of `V`. The hypothesis `he : e ∈ T.edgeSet` forces `V` to have at least two distinct vertices. In a connected graph on such a `V`, every vertex has a neighbour, so its support is all of `V`.

That makes `T1.support` and `T2.support` both equal to `Set.univ`. Since `V` is nonempty, they cannot be disjoint. For example, take `T` to be the path on two vertices and `e` its one edge. The hypotheses hold, but no `T1` and `T2` satisfy the conclusion.

I did not change `/work/combi_brualdi_ch11_59.lean`; it still contains the original `sorry`. The informal claim is true, but it needs trees on the two components' vertex sets rather than on all of `V`. That would mean changing the statement, which the rules don't allow.
